A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAG-WM work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching despite v4's added methodological sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original watermarking and tamper-localization experiments, baseline comparisons, sampling/DVRD ablations, and degradation robustness results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and additionally reports an empirically measured intrinsic localization-watermark error rate in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: v3 already identifies DMJS, WLR, DVRD, and TAD and evaluates both sampling strategies and DVRD variants. v4 Section 4 supplies their previously missing construction details; it does not establish a replacement component or changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same prompt dataset, Stable Diffusion versions, training manipulations, four inpainting evaluation scenarios, foreground/background tampering, and clean/degraded conditions. Appendices A–B retain the same degradation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: DwtDct, DwtDctSvd, RivaGAN, EditGuard, Stable Signature, Tree-Ring, and Gaussian Shading in the general comparison; Gaussian Shading and EditGuard in tampering curves; and EditGuard in localization comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 Section 4.3 adds the conditional localization-bit mismatch rate in untampered regions at θ=0.5 as a diagnostic metric. Existing benchmark metrics, splits, sampling/inversion settings, and training budgets remain unchanged. The new diagnostic's sample size and measurement procedure are unspecified.

E4.justification: v4 Section 4.3 adds a limited error analysis contrasting empirically measured intrinsic localization-bit errors with the modeled tampering error rate to support detection. The sampling/DVRD ablation, visual cases, and Appendix B robustness sweeps are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ten-batch CLIP-score comparison, reported ± values, and t-tests. v4's additional intrinsic-error estimate supplies no new repeated-run information, uncertainty interval, or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v4 Section 4.3 newly reports an intrinsic localization-bit error probability of 0.14513 at θ=0.5. Numerical entries in v3 Tables 1–3 match v4 Tables 2–4, and the retained experimental figures, including Appendix B, contain unchanged results.

T1.justification: v4 adds formal development absent from v3: the DDIM inversion approximation, watermark and sampling definitions, the distribution-preservation derivation in Equations 6–9, and the tampering-error model yielding 2θ(1−θ) in Equations 10–11. These substantially expand the mathematical account.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint copyright protection and localization, lossless generation quality, 256-bit capacity, robustness, and efficiency. The new method exposition and derivations support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive rationale linking spatial inversion behavior to localization, fewer sampling boundaries to reduced errors, and learned DVRD processing to avoiding manual kernel selection. Existing interpretations of benchmark results and limitations concerning schedulers, global attacks, and fixed seeds remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly documents message repetition, ChaCha20 encryption, sampling boundaries, XOR mask construction, convolutional/UNet DVRD implementations, VAE mask decoding with a zero threshold, and selective majority voting. This substantially improves implementation information; existing training settings and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Bernstein's ChaCha reference to support the encryption description. The existing cited works and positioning relative to generative watermarking and tamper-localization research are retained; other citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v3 proceeds directly from related work to experiments. v4 inserts organized preliminaries and a four-part method explanation, substantially completing the paper's explanatory structure. Existing experimental prose, conclusions, and appendix discussions are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v4 adds an end-to-end framework diagram, paired sampling-strategy diagrams, and a sampling-boundary table as Figures 1–2 and Table 1. These substantially expand the visual explanation of the method. Existing experimental displays are retained and renumbered, with the appendix plot relocated beside its discussion.

improvement.justification: v3 names the method's components and reports results but omits their construction. v4 Sections 3–4 supply the missing specification, mathematical rationale, and explanatory diagrams, resolving a central deficiency in technical completeness and reproducibility while retaining the experimental evidence. The added Section 4.1 prose contains a duplicated bit-pair inconsistent with Figure 2 and Table 1, but this localized defect does not outweigh the substantial documentation gains.
